clue.text: Model texted "thank you", a line on back of photo?

indicators.note: placed on the back of means coming after the photo piece in the answer

parts.note: in text-message shorthand thank you is written TY
a photo is a pic

explanation.surface: Someone captions a snapshot with a texted thanks and wonders if that is normal behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is an adjective here, as in a model example; 'on back of' tells you A and L come after PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something model is a perfect specimen of its kind, a textbook or representative instance.

clue.text: Nice break-up technique? Shit happens

explanation.surface: A comment on ending a relationship politely, followed by a shrug of resignation.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice (said 'neece', like the French city) is a British coconut biscuit, so a Nice biscuit breaking up is a crumbling cookie; the capital N disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying shrugs at misfortune as inevitable, and one way a Nice biscuit falls apart is literal crumbling.

clue.text: Teletubby drawn in school

parts.note: Po is the smallest, red Teletubby in the children's TV show
D stands for drawn in tables of sports results

explanation.surface: A children's TV character is sketched by pupils in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' looks like sketched but is the results-table D; 'school' is a group of whales or dolphins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a group of marine mammals such as whales, the same collective sense as a school of fish.

clue.text: Cold range of trimmed sausage

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: trimmed tells you to cut the last letter off the word for range

parts.note: the horizon marks the furthest range of vision

explanation.surface: A deli counter offers a chilled selection of cut sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy cured pork sausage from Spain, flavoured with paprika.

clue.text: Attraction of power changing hands?

indicators.note: hands here are the left and right letters, so the R and the L swap places in the word for power

parts.note: to rule is to hold power, and rule is authority or power

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a transfer of political power is what makes it appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' means R (right) and L (left) swap places in RULE, giving LURE; the surface suggests a change of ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is a temptation or enticement that draws someone in.

clue.text: Firm bottom (rude)

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
arse is British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A firmly toned rear end, with a bracketed warning that the word is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSE is the British vulgar word for bottom, which makes the bracketed '(rude)' a self-aware joke as well as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse language is vulgar, crude and impolite.

clue.text: Balance is awkward to spacemen

indicators.note: awkward signals that the letters of to spacemen are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Astronauts find staying upright difficult in zero gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: To balance something is to offset or make up for it, as when one quantity counterweighs another.

clue.text: Dirty deal to imprison judge suggested

indicators.note: to imprison means the letters for judge are locked inside the rearranged deal
dirty suggests the letters of deal are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
LUD is the judge as in 'm'lud', the courtroom form of address

explanation.surface: A corrupt bargain to have a judge jailed was hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' scrambles to ALDE, and 'to imprison' locks the court's form of address (as in 'm'lud') inside; 'Dirty deal' reads as a corrupt bargain, hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to hint at something indirectly, so alluded and hinted are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Bloody good uni opening as one uni's demolished

indicators.note: demolished means the collected letters are knocked down and rebuilt in a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of uni

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
taken as written, with its S, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A good new university opens while another institution is knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' scrambles G, U (from 'uni opening'), ASONE and UNIS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or involving blood, the word is a formal synonym of bloody or bloodthirsty.

clue.text: See 1 Down
Hearing test result involving old Golf in car crash

indicators.note: in means the letters for old and Golf sit inside the car crash pieces

parts.note: an Audi is a German make of car
to ram is to crash into something
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Testing hearing after an elderly VW Golf is involved in a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is also a Volkswagen car, which makes 'car crash' read naturally; here it is the phonetic-alphabet G.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiogram is the chart produced by a hearing test, plotting what pitches a patient can detect.

clue.text: Left bar — no time for local talk

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is dropped from the bar

parts.note: an ingot is a bar of metal

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the pub without time for a chat with the regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is a metal INGOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is the jargon or dialect spoken by a particular group or place.

clue.text: Bird one's spotted in hide

indicators.note: spotted in means the letters for one's are seen inside the hide

parts.note: a hide is an animal skin
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's report that one bird has been seen from the hide.
explanation.walkthrough: A hide is a birdwatching shelter, so the surface is natural; here it is SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: With foreign money to invest I'll back King George winner — in this?

definitions.text: With foreign money to invest I'll back King George winner — in this?

indicators.note: to invest means the reversed letters are wrapped inside the foreign money

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

indicators.note: back here means the letters of I'll are taken in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written, without its apostrophe
GR stands for Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George
an ace is a winning shot or a winner

explanation.surface: A punter with foreign cash says they will bet on a big-race winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes LLI, and 'to invest' wraps the Japanese coin round it. The King George is a famous British horse race; in a selling race the winner is auctioned afterwards, so money to invest buys the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of horse race the winning horse must be offered for sale at auction after the race.

clue.text: One goes nowhere if very wet?

definitions.text: One goes nowhere if very wet?

parts.words: One goes nowhere if very wet?
parts.note: very wet weather is proverbially lovely for ducks, so a duck that stays put in it must be lifeless; and a plan going nowhere is doomed

explanation.surface: Someone stays indoors whenever it pours.
explanation.definitionFit: A doomed project or person with no prospects is said to be a failure beyond saving.

clue.text: Independent -like Metro — can rely mostly on distribution

parts.note: Metro is a free daily newspaper handed out in Britain

indicators.note: on distribution means the letters are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of rely is dropped

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor muses that the Independent, like the free Metro, depends on getting handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RELY to REL, and 'on distribution' rearranges CAN plus REL into LANCER. Metro is a free British commuter paper, so the clue cutely calls a freelance an Independent.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for themselves rather than for one employer, so is self-employed.

clue.text: Once filled, share out student accommodation

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Once the rooms are taken, students divide up the shared housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A university building where students live, typically in their first year.

clue.text: Blow-by-blow description of calls?

parts.note: read literally, a trip made of brief calls at many places, each marked by a blast on a train whistle

explanation.surface: A detailed account of a series of phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast journey with many brief stops, typical of election campaigners on trains.

clue.text: Scenery over in Spain will be part of mosaic

indicators.note: over means the word for scenery is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a stage set is theatrical scenery
sera is Spanish for will be

explanation.surface: Stage scenery shipped to Spain will become part of a decorative mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SET into TES; the Spanish future tense of ser gives SERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles of stone or glass set into a mosaic.

clue.text: Quietly wind up loads of lines

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: loads means the word of is loaded into the word for wind up

parts.note: to wind someone up is to rile them

explanation.surface: Gently cranking up a machine that churns out lines of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like the ending of something but is RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is an outline, the lines of a face seen from the side.

clue.text: Old European bloke recalled huge bathroom

indicators.note: recalled means the word for bloke is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: a guy is a bloke
OS is outsize, the clothing label for huge
lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a man with an enormous bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses GUY to YUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the former Balkan federation that broke up in the 1990s, so an old nationality.

clue.text: Dame Edna's friend not completely la-di-da, some said

indicators.note: not completely means the last letter of the word for la-di-da is dropped

parts.note: posh and la-di-da both mean affectedly upper-class

indicators.note: said means the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: some is pronounced the same as sum

explanation.surface: A drag star's chum is only partly snobbish, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edna Everage, Barry Humphries' character, greeted her audience as her possums.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edna's catchphrase was 'Hello, possums', an affectionate term for her fans.

clue.text: Vocal style primarily associated with jazz fan

definitions.text: Vocal style primarily associated with jazz fan

indicators.note: primarily means take just the first letter of style

parts.note: cat is old jazz slang for a fan or musician

explanation.surface: A singing style closely linked to a jazz enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: S from 'style primarily' plus CAT for 'jazz fan'; the whole clue also describes the improvised wordless singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised nonsense-syllable singing, made famous by Ella Fitzgerald and Louis Armstrong.

clue.text: A voice without substance after helium gag

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the helium symbol

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

indicators.note: without substance means the middle of voice is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A squeaky helium-voiced joke falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke but means retch. Helium makes voices squeaky, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to retch or try to vomit.

clue.text: Red dye, product of mine, coating crest

indicators.note: coating means the mine product wraps around the word for crest

parts.note: coal is dug from a mine
a chine is a ridge or crest of land

explanation.surface: A red pigment from one's own mine is used to paint a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson colouring made from crushed insects, used in food.

clue.text: Wood panel made to hide it

indicators.note: the phrase panel made is made to hide the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: A wooden panel built to conceal something.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood tree and its timber.

clue.text: Theatre's atmosphere or condition

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a theatre's mood or its physical state matters more.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair means state of upkeep, as in a house in good or poor shape.

clue.text: The Jolly Sailor's first bottle initially opened for one taking drink

indicators.note: bottle is a verb here, meaning to hold the letter for opened inside the run before it

parts.note: taken as written
a jolly is naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of Sailor's
initially means take the opening letter of opened

explanation.surface: At the Jolly Sailor pub the first bottle of the night is opened for a drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a noun but means contain. A jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine; The Jolly Sailor sounds like a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask holds hot or cold drinks, so it is a vessel that takes in liquid.
